title: A Hollow for the Choir
premise: In the city of Vellamarch, where magic was outlawed after the gods fell silent, Petra Whitlock has survived twenty years by hiding her beast-speaker gift behind a shopfront of harmless charms. When prayers begin to be answered again—wildly, wrongly, by something wearing the old gods' names—Petra learns the covenant between realms was not broken but stolen, and that her mother was one of the thieves. To stop the false god from consuming both worlds, Petra must gather the scattered choir-stones, confront the truth of her family's betrayal, and choose between exposing herself to execution or letting the last true god die unheard. In the end she reforges the covenant at terrible cost: her gift is given back to the beasts themselves, and she finally belongs—not as a speaker for them, but as one voice among many.
about_author: L. M. Brightwater is the pen name of a former field biologist who spent years recording birdsong in vanishing wetlands before turning to fiction. They write about voices the world refuses to hear, and live quietly somewhere with too many animals.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Quiet
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. We meet her stall, her careful smallness, and the stray dog she secretly converses with each evening. A customer's prayer is answered impossibly before her eyes. Emotional beat: the unease of a hidden life beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The city's rats speak of a 'second sun' beneath the cathedral ruins; other beasts have gone silent or mad. Petra investigates against her instincts and finds a shrine where an old god's name answers back—with her own mother's voice. Beat: dread entwined with longing.

chapters.title: A Debt in Ash
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. She seeks out Brother Anselm, a disgraced priest who once recorded the covenant rites. He reveals the Hollowing: twenty years ago the gods' chorus was severed, and someone stole the first stone. Beat: grief for a history she never knew she inherited.

chapters.title: The Warden's Question
chapters.summary: Warden Ilsa Corvane's POV. The magic-inquisition's sharpest hunter notices charms working that shouldn't, and begins pulling threads toward the market district. Beat: cold competence masking doubt about the regime she serves.

chapters.title: Choir-Stone, First Verse
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Guided by the dog and a dying hawk, she retrieves the first choir-stone from a flooded cistern, nearly drowning as the false god whispers offers of safety. Beat: first taste of real power—and real danger.

chapters.title: Old Friends, New Prices
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Her oldest friend Tam, a fence with debts, sells information about a 'witch in the market' to survive. Petra forgives him and lies to him in the same breath. Beat: loyalty bending under fear.

chapters.title: The God That Answers Wrong
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He documents answered prayers across the city: healings that hollow the healed, blessings that take memories as payment. He realizes the entity is building a congregation out of the desperate. Beat: scholarly horror becoming personal resolve.

chapters.title: Mother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In her mother's sealed effects she finds the theft recorded plainly: three conspirators, one stone kept as insurance—the Whitlock name on every line. Beat: identity shattered; the hunted discovers she is also heir to the crime.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa arrests Tam and questions him gently, expertly. He gives her nothing but a description that could be half the city. Beat: unexpected respect between hunter and the hunted's friend.

chapters.title: The Second Stone Sings
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Hidden in a plague-crypt, the second stone resonates with her bloodline and shows her a memory: her mother weeping as she cut the covenant, believing she was saving the world from the gods' demands. Beat: sympathy complicating anger.

chapters.title: Beasts at the Gate
chapters.summary: Multiple beast-voices, channeled through Petra. The city's animals, driven restless by the false god, mass at the walls; the Wardens plan a cull. Petra must use her gift publicly to turn them—or watch a massacre. Beat: invisibility ends here.

chapters.title: Witch of the Market
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa witnesses Petra calming the beasts and has her dead to rights—yet lets her walk, haunted by what the beasts showed her of the Hollowing. Beat: loyalty to law cracking against witnessed truth.

chapters.title: The Third Stone Is a Person
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The final stone was never hidden—it lives inside Anselm, implanted by the conspirators to keep it beyond reach. Telling him means telling him he is a vessel built to die when the covenant is remade. Beat: truth as cruelty and mercy at once.

chapters.title: Anselm's Choice
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. He wrestles with being a man whose whole faithful life was scaffolding around a stone. He chooses to carry it to the rite anyway, asking only that his records survive him. Beat: quiet, devastating devotion.

chapters.title: What the False God Offers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The entity corners her in dreams, offering her mother back, her anonymity back, the beasts' voices forever—if she simply stops. For one chapter she almost says yes. Beat: temptation rendered tender.

chapters.title: Tam's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. To redeem himself, Tam sells the false god's cult false information about the rite's location, knowing they'll kill him if discovered. Beat: a small man making a large choice.

chapters.title: The Cathedral of Roots
chapters.summary: Petra, Anselm, and Ilsa converge beneath the ruined cathedral where the covenant was first sung. The false god wears the assembled faces of everyone its 'blessings' emptied. Beat: dread at the threshold of the climax.

chapters.title: Requiem, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Climax begins. The rite requires a voice for each realm—human, beast, divine. Cultists and Wardens collide overhead while below, the false god unmakes Anselm's memories mid-rite. Beat: everything unraveling at once.

chapters.title: Every Voice at Once
chapters.summary: Climax. Petra does the forbidden thing: instead of speaking for the beasts, she opens herself fully and lets all their voices speak through her, joining the chorus. The true god answers; the false one, revealed as the severed half of the covenant, is sung back into wholeness rather than destroyed. Beat: transcendence through surrender of self.

chapters.title: The Price of the Song
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The covenant holds—but it took Anselm's life, Ilsa's career, and Petra's gift, returned to the beasts who now choose whether to speak to her at all. Beat: mourning braided with awe.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Bells
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Magic is no longer outlawed but licensed to the wary; Ilsa resigns rather than enforce the new compromise, and visits Tam's grave. Beat: bittersweet order rising from ruin.

chapters.title: A Hollow, Filled
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Epilogue: her stall reopens, selling honest nothing. One morning the dog returns and speaks her name—not because she commands it, but because it chooses to. Beat: belonging earned, at last, freely given.
